A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a neural network designed to recognize local patterns in grid-like data, especially images. Instead of connecting every image pixel to every detector, it uses [[Convolution]]: sliding a small calculation across the image to examine one region at a time.

The calculation uses a [[Kernel]], a small grid of learned numbers that responds to a particular pattern, such as a vertical edge. Applying one kernel across an image produces a [[Feature Map]], a grid showing where that pattern appears strongly. An [[Activation Function]] then keeps useful signals or changes them nonlinearly, allowing the network to learn more than simple combinations.

CNNs often use [[Pooling]] to shrink feature maps while preserving important signals. For example, when recognizing a handwritten “7,” early layers may detect edges, later layers may combine them into corners and strokes, and deeper layers may identify the complete digit. Because the same kernel is reused across the image, a CNN can recognize a feature wherever it appears while using fewer learned numbers than a fully connected network.
